interactions.title: Binary search, one comparison at a time
interactions.description: Watch lo, mid and hi close in on the answer. Switch to lower/upper bound to see the half-open template, or type your own array and target.

questions.prompt: Why does the lesson write `mid = lo + (hi - lo) / 2` instead of `(lo + hi) / 2`?
options: It rounds toward the right half
`lo + hi` can overflow `int` for large indices
It is faster on most CPUs
questions.explanation: When `lo + hi` exceeds `Integer.MAX_VALUE` the sum wraps to a negative number. `hi - lo` never overflows, so the midpoint stays correct.

questions.prompt: At most how many comparisons does the classic binary search need on 1,000,000 sorted elements?
What is the lower bound (first index with `a[i] >= 6`) in `[1, 3, 5, 7, 9]`?
questions.explanation: `a[3] = 7` is the first element ≥ 6. 6 is not present, and 3 is exactly where it would be inserted to keep the array sorted.
When the key is missing, `Arrays.binarySearch` returns `-(insertionPoint) - 1`. 4 would be inserted at index 2, so the result is −2 − 1 = −3.

interactions.title: Sort it step by step
interactions.description: Every comparison and move, with counters. Duplicates are lettered (5ᵃ, 5ᵇ) so you can see which algorithms are stable. Try a sorted or reversed array too.

interactions.title: Flashcards: sorting algorithms at a glance
interactions.description: Say the time, space and stability out loud before flipping.

cards.back: Best O(n) with the early-exit check, average and worst O(n²). O(1) space. **Stable.**
O(n²) comparisons in every case, but at most n − 1 swaps. O(1) space. **Not stable.**
Best O(n) on sorted input, worst O(n²). O(1) space. **Stable.** Excellent for small or nearly sorted arrays.
O(n log n) in every case. O(n) extra space for arrays. **Stable.**
Average O(n log n), worst O(n²) (bad pivots). O(log n) stack on average. **Not stable.**
O(n log n) in every case. O(1) extra space. **Not stable.**
Primitives: dual-pivot quicksort (stability doesn't matter for primitives). Objects: TimSort, which is **stable**.

interactions.title: Traverse the tree yourself
interactions.description: Preorder, inorder and postorder are the same recursion — only the moment of “output” changes. Level order swaps the call stack for a queue.
